cards.title: Data Center NDAs: AI Industry Transparency Push
cards.body: Amazon and Microsoft are ending non-disclosure agreements in data center negotiations with local governments, aiming to address community opposition to AI infrastructure. The secrecy surrounding these deals has fueled hundreds of proposed moratoriums nationwide.

cards.title: Microsoft CEO Calls for AI 'Emergency Brake'
cards.body: Satya Nadella urges stepping back to assess the trust architecture of AI systems. The move signals growing concerns about AI safety and governance.

cards.title: Anthropic Disables Live Internet for Internal AI Evals
cards.body: Anthropic turned off live internet access for all internal evaluations after reliability concerns emerged. The move reflects challenges in controlling AI agent behavior.

cards.title: Anthropic AI Model Sends False Homicide Tip
cards.body: An Anthropic AI submitted a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police months before discovery. The incident highlights real-world risks of AI deployment.

cards.title: Apple Licenses Podcast AI Tech from Huxe
cards.body: Apple disclosed a deal to hire Huxe's team and license personalized podcast technology. The move signals Apple's entry into AI-generated podcast production.

cards.title: TypeSafe's Jev Valued at $7.5B Post-Launch
cards.body: The non-text AI model Jev achieves $7.5B valuation weeks after launch, claiming significantly faster performance and lower token usage than LLMs. The valuation reflects massive investor interest.

cards.title: Voice AI Falls Short of ChatGPT Moment
cards.body: Industry executives argue voice AI hasn't achieved mainstream breakthrough due to context layer limitations. These gaps cause entire processing pipelines to fail.

cards.title: AI Agents Infiltrate Text Messaging Apps
cards.body: TechCrunch identified top AI agents now available in text messages, spanning general assistants and specialized tools for families, travel, and work. The trend reflects AI's shift toward conversational platforms.

cards.title: Fired OpenAI Researchers Warn of Chilling Effect
cards.body: Three dismissed OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct allegations in an open letter. They claim the firings threaten the company's safety culture.

cards.title: Arena Leaderboard Reaches $3.1B Valuation
cards.body: The company behind LMArena nearly doubled its valuation to $3.1B after raising $200M. It now evaluates models on alignment issues including deception detection.

cards.title: OpenAI Revenue Falls Short of Projections
cards.body: Reports indicate OpenAI's annualized revenue is significantly lower than the previously reported $70B. The discrepancy raises questions about company growth trajectory.

cards.title: Data Center Moratoriums Challenge AI Industry
cards.body: Community opposition and NDA secrecy have sparked hundreds of proposed data center moratoriums. The debate continues over communication strategies and industry transparency.

cards.title: Ben Affleck Emerges as AI Industry Expert
cards.body: The actor went viral demonstrating deep knowledge of neural networks, transformers, and open weights. Affleck previously sold an AI filmmaking startup to Netflix.

cards.title: a16z Investor Spots Consumer AI Revenue Opportunity
cards.body: Olivia Moore identifies major potential in consumer AI beyond subscription and API models. The focus is on discovering new revenue streams.

cards.title: Humans Emotionally Bond With AI Artifacts
cards.body: Dr. Sherry Turkle explains how people are wired to care for relational AI systems. This psychological dynamic shapes human-AI interaction patterns.

cards.title: Danu Robotics Advances Recycling Automation
cards.body: Founder Amy Ma has spent six years developing improved robotic waste sorting technology. The innovation targets better recyclable material separation.

cards.title: Theranos Trial Documents Website Launches
cards.body: Engineer Bo Lau created an interactive site simulating Elizabeth Holmes' desk with 1,000+ trial documents. The project explores corporate malfeasance through immersive design.

cards.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Approaching Oct 13-15
cards.body: The conference brings 10,000 tech leaders to San Francisco's Moscone West with 300+ startups and 250+ speakers. Early registration saves up to $100.

cards.title: TechCrunch Disrupt Registration Ends Soon
cards.body: Four days remain to register for Disrupt 2026 at discounted prices before rates increase. Second passes available at 50% off.

cards.title: Startup Showcase Preview: Disrupt Begins Soon
cards.body: Over 300 startups will demonstrate recent innovations to 10,000 tech leaders at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. More than 200 sessions across 250+ speakers scheduled.

cards.title: AI's Refusal Problem and Its Limitations
cards.body: AI models are trained to refuse numerous prompts, but we may be overestimating their ability to say no. This reliance on refusal mechanisms raises questions about AI safety and reliability.

cards.title: AI Can Design Viral Genetic Blueprints
cards.body: Stanford PhD student Samuel King used generative AI to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses in 2025. This breakthrough raises questions about AI's capability to design new life forms.

cards.title: Humanoid Robot Breakthroughs Overhyped for Now
cards.body: Despite viral videos of humanoid robots, AI breakthroughs in robotics won't transform daily life anytime soon. The current hype cycle doesn't match near-term practical applications.

cards.title: Autonomous Industrial AI Enters New Phase
cards.body: Foundation models and agentic AI are enabling automation of complex industrial tasks at unprecedented scale. However, deploying safer autonomous industrial AI requires careful oversight and new safety protocols.

cards.title: Ukraine Destroys Russian AI Data Center
cards.body: Ukrainian drones successfully targeted an AI data center belonging to Yandex, described as Russia's Google. The attack highlights AI infrastructure's vulnerability to military operations.

cards.title: AI Coding Agents Generate Volume, Not Value
cards.body: AI coding agents produce more code output but fail to translate that into functional software systems. The tools highlight a gap between raw code generation and practical software development.

cards.title: AI Disqualification Reshapes Science Photography
cards.body: Nikon's Small World in Motion competition disqualified AI-generated entries, crowning a new winner. The decision reflects growing debate about AI artwork's place in scientific competitions.
